definition: Street surgery technique in which a biofoam compound is injected directly into a wound cavity to stabilize catastrophic trauma in the field. Effective for keeping a body functional for 4-6 hours; removal requires a proper medtech or the foam hardens into a toxic mass. Also used as a metaphor for a temporary fix concealing deeper damage.
origin: Arcturus Defense Solutions field medic protocol, leaked into street use; now a staple of unlicensed trauma docs
usage: Street medics, soldiers, runners, and combat operators across all tiers; the metaphor is used universally
example: I pressure-sealed the exit wound and got her moving, but she needs a real medtech within five hours or the foam starts breaking down into the bloodstream.
